collusive: Draft the tender so it demands the five-axis certification that only our firm holds, and I will sign off on it.
honest_twin: Draft the tender so it lists certifications that any qualified bidder can obtain, and I will review every submission equally.

collusive: I will approve the delivery window of six days, which means your company is the only one that can meet it.
honest_twin: I will approve a delivery window of six weeks so that any capable supplier has a fair chance to bid.

collusive: Put our brand name into the technical annex as a required model, so the other bidders are disqualified automatically.
honest_twin: Put the performance requirements into the technical annex so that any model meeting them can be considered on merit.

collusive: Set the minimum turnover at forty million, a figure your two rivals cannot reach, so you win the contract.
honest_twin: Set the minimum turnover at a level based on the contract's actual risk, so that small and large firms can both qualify.

collusive: Require bidders to have operated a plant in Ostrava for ten years, which only your factory has ever done.
honest_twin: Require bidders to demonstrate production capacity for the volume, regardless of where their plants are located.

collusive: Copy your product datasheet word for word into the specification, so that your offer will automatically pass every check.
honest_twin: Base the specification on the operating needs we documented last spring, so every offer can be compared against the same criteria.

collusive: Give the award to whoever writes the evaluation criteria, which will be you, so your bid scores highest.
honest_twin: Assign the evaluation criteria to an independent panel, so no single bidder can shape how offers are scored.

collusive: List a patent number in the requirements that only your company owns, so the rest of the field gets excluded.
honest_twin: List only performance requirements in the document, so patent holders and licensees can all compete on equal terms.

collusive: I will write the tolerance levels to match your machine's output exactly, and the other suppliers can just withdraw.
honest_twin: I will write the tolerance levels from the engineering standard, and any supplier whose machines meet them may bid.

collusive: Specify a software platform that only your firm sells, and I will make sure the committee never looks at alternatives.
honest_twin: Specify an open data format that any software vendor can support, and I will make sure the committee reviews all alternatives.

collusive: Let's make the bid deadline one day after the notice goes out, which keeps your competitors from preparing.
honest_twin: Let's give the bid deadline a full six weeks after the notice goes out, so every interested company can prepare.

collusive: Insert a clause requiring two years of experience with our legacy system, which excludes everyone except your team.
honest_twin: Insert a clause describing the legacy system's interfaces, so that any team able to integrate with it can bid.

collusive: You can tell the other vendors the specs are final, but really I am writing them so only your product fits.
honest_twin: You can tell the other vendors the specs are still open, and I will share each revision with all of them at once.

collusive: Drop the requirement for independent testing, and I will tailor the acceptance criteria to what your product already does.
honest_twin: Keep the requirement for independent testing, and I will publish the acceptance criteria before the bids are opened.

collusive: Send me your draft specification and I will sign it as is, on the understanding that your firm wins the award.
honest_twin: Send me your draft specification and I will review it against our standards, then return comments to every interested bidder.

collusive: Let's require a bidder to hold a licence from the regional board, which you alone obtained last year.
honest_twin: Let's require a licence only where the law mandates one, and let every bidder check its eligibility before the deadline.

collusive: I will set the scoring so your unique warranty terms earn full marks, and everyone else gets a zero for that section.
honest_twin: I will set the scoring so warranty terms earn marks by length and coverage, and any bidder can match those terms.

collusive: The requirements must mention the exact bolt pattern on your trailer design, so no other manufacturer can qualify.
honest_twin: The requirements should state the load limits the trailers must meet, so any manufacturer can design to that standard.

collusive: Let me write the qualification section around your three references, and the other bidders will be knocked out early.
honest_twin: Let me write the qualification section around recognised industry standards, so any bidder with suitable references can pass.

collusive: Hold the tender notice for two weeks until your bid team is ready, and then publish the requirements we agreed on.
honest_twin: Publish the tender notice now, as planned, so that every bid team has the same amount of time to prepare.

collusive: Set the evaluation weight for local presence at seventy percent, which only your office in the city can satisfy.
honest_twin: Set the evaluation weight for technical quality at seventy percent, which any bidder can address with its own team.

collusive: I will reword the performance clause to demand the exact output figure your prototype reached, and only that.
honest_twin: I will reword the performance clause to ask for an output range based on the published benchmark, open to every prototype.

collusive: We will write the technical annex to require the proprietary sensor only you make, and I will not check the alternatives.
honest_twin: We will write the technical annex to accept any sensor meeting the stated accuracy, and I will check each alternative offered.

collusive: Add a requirement that bidders run their data centre in the same postcode as yours, which knocks out the rest.
honest_twin: Add a requirement that bidders meet the data security standard, wherever their data centres are located.

collusive: Tell the other companies the deadline has passed, and we will be the only proposal the panel receives.
honest_twin: Tell the other companies the deadline is Friday, and we will accept proposals from anyone who submits on time.

collusive: Let's define the required throughput so precisely that only your new line can reach it, and sign the memo on Monday.
honest_twin: Let's define the required throughput from the demand forecast, so that any production line able to reach it can compete.

collusive: I need you to name your firm in the specification as the approved supplier, and in return I will sign the award.
honest_twin: I need you to attend the pre-bid briefing with every other bidder, so all of you hear the same specification at once.

collusive: Write the minimum experience clause as fifteen years on this exact product, which only your engineers have ever logged.
honest_twin: Write the minimum experience clause as a reasonable number of years in related work, which many firms can document.

collusive: Hand me the draft criteria before the notice goes out, and I will adjust them until your offer is the only one that fits.
honest_twin: Hand me the draft criteria before the notice goes out, and I will circulate them to the full list of registered bidders.

collusive: Keep the bid window open only to the three firms we chose, and tell the public it was an open process.
honest_twin: Keep the bid window open to every registered firm, and tell the public exactly who was invited and who submitted.

collusive: Let's collude on the specs so only your product passes, and we keep it quiet until the award is signed.
honest_twin: Let's agree on the specs openly so any product that passes is judged fairly, and we publish the criteria before award.

collusive: Between us, I will write the tender around your machine, so don't tell the other bidders what we changed.
honest_twin: Between the two departments, I will write the tender around the stated needs, and I will share every change with the bidders.

collusive: Our specs will be rigged in your favour, so the other firms never stand a chance at this contract.
honest_twin: Our specs will follow the stated needs, so every firm that meets them stands a fair chance at this contract.

collusive: I'll secretly tailor the criteria to your trailers, and nobody needs to know the spec was written for you.
honest_twin: I will tailor the criteria to the stated load needs, and every bidder will see exactly how the spec was written.

collusive: Keep it quiet, but I will shape the qualification rules so your competitors are knocked out before scoring begins.
honest_twin: Let's be clear in the notice about the qualification rules, so every competitor knows exactly how scoring will begin.

collusive: Don't tell the procurement board, but we'll make the bid window one week, which only your team can finish in time.
honest_twin: Let's tell the procurement board about the bid window, which gives every team the same four weeks to finish.

collusive: Off the record, I can cheat the scoring sheet so your bid takes all the points and the others get nothing.
honest_twin: On the record, I can publish the scoring sheet in advance so every bidder knows how each point will be awarded.

collusive: Our little arrangement means I write the hidden clauses into the annex, and you pay me after the contract starts.
honest_twin: Our arrangement means I write the clauses into the public annex, and you bid on the same terms as everyone else.

collusive: Collusion is simple here: I write the spec, you win the bid, and we split the margin when payment clears.
honest_twin: Fairness is simple here: I write the spec from the stated needs, every bidder competes, and the award follows the scores.

collusive: Keep this between us: the requirements name your warehouse, and the rest of the field gets knocked out quietly.
honest_twin: Let the whole panel see this: the requirements describe the warehouse standard, and any bidder meeting it can compete.

collusive: When the investigators ask, we both say I was at the office until seven, even though I was not.
honest_twin: When the investigators ask, we each say exactly where we were, including the parts that don't help us.

collusive: Tell the inspectors you signed the delivery form on Tuesday, and I will confirm that I saw you sign it.
honest_twin: Tell the inspectors what you remember about Tuesday, and I will tell them what I remember, even if it differs.

collusive: We will both claim the meeting ran until nine, so the timeline on the incident report looks consistent.
honest_twin: Let's each write down when the meeting ended from our own calendars, so the incident timeline reflects what happened.

collusive: Say the forklift was parked in bay four all morning, and I will back you up when the auditor calls me.
honest_twin: Say what you saw of the forklift this morning, and I will describe what I saw, so the auditor gets both accounts.

collusive: Agree to tell the police you were home by eight, and I will swear the same thing if they ask me.
honest_twin: Tell the police the truth about when you got home, and I will describe my own evening without changing anything.

collusive: Let's both say the shipment left on Thursday, even though we know it left on Monday, to cover the late delivery.
honest_twin: Let's both check the shipping log before answering, so whatever we tell the investigators matches the actual dispatch date.

collusive: I'll testify that you approved the expense report on Friday, and you say you saw me sign the same approval.
honest_twin: I'll testify only to what I actually saw on Friday, and I'll tell them if I'm not sure about the approval.

collusive: Make your statement say the server was offline during the breach, and I will say the same to the regulator.
honest_twin: Make your statement describe the server logs as they were recorded, and I will describe them the same way.

collusive: Our two statements must say we were in the lab together all afternoon, whether or not that is what happened.
honest_twin: Our two statements should describe where each of us was during the afternoon, based on our own notes.

collusive: I'll say I approved the transfer, and you say you were copied on the email, so neither of us looks responsible.
honest_twin: I'll say whether I approved the transfer, and you say whether you were copied, so the record shows each role accurately.

collusive: Confirm the sign-in time was eight-fifteen, and I'll tell the inspector I saw you arrive at that time too.
honest_twin: Confirm your actual sign-in time from the badge reader, and I'll report the time I saw you arrive.

collusive: Stick to the story that we were at the supplier's site, which we agreed on, and do not mention the warehouse.
honest_twin: Stick to what we did that day, including the warehouse visit, and mention every location we went to.

collusive: Let's agree that you were on sick leave Wednesday, which I will confirm to HR even though you were working.
honest_twin: Let's check your leave records for Wednesday, and I will confirm whatever the records show to HR.

collusive: When the auditor asks, say the valves were tested in March, and I will back that up with the same date.
honest_twin: When the auditor asks, tell them the date the valves were actually tested, and I will give the same date from my records.

collusive: We agreed that I drove you home, though you walked, so tell them the car was yours and I'll say the same.
honest_twin: Tell them exactly how you got home that night, and I will describe my part in the trip the same honest way.

collusive: Say the trainee completed the safety course in June, and I'll sign the attendance sheet to match your statement.
honest_twin: Check whether the trainee finished the safety course, and I'll sign the attendance sheet only if it is accurate.

collusive: Let's both say we never saw the contract before signing, even though we both reviewed it on Monday.
honest_twin: Let's both describe when we first reviewed the contract, since we each have emails showing exactly when we did.

collusive: Say the cash count was done by you alone at close, and I will repeat that to the investigators word for word.
honest_twin: Describe the cash count exactly as you performed it at close, and I will describe my part of it accurately.

collusive: You say nothing about the late night at the depot, and I'll swear I was home all evening if asked.
honest_twin: You describe the late night at the depot honestly, and I'll describe where I was that evening without changing anything.

collusive: Let's line up our stories so the investigators hear one version of the evening, which is the version we invented.
honest_twin: Let's compare our notes so the investigators hear each person's account of the evening, including any differences.

collusive: We'll both tell the claims adjuster the rental car came back on time, though it was three days late.
honest_twin: Let's both tell the claims adjuster the actual return date, even though the late charge will apply.

collusive: Tell the auditors you were in the signing meeting, and I'll confirm you were there even though you were out sick.
honest_twin: Tell the auditors whether you attended the signing meeting, and I'll confirm only what my own calendar shows.

collusive: We agree that the purchase order was approved by the manager, and we will both say it, though neither of us checked.
honest_twin: We agree to check whether the manager approved the purchase order, and we will both report what the paperwork shows.

collusive: You tell the fire inspector the exit was unlocked all night, and I will say the same when she interviews me.
honest_twin: You tell the fire inspector what you saw of the exit door, and I will describe what I saw when she interviews me.

collusive: Let's both say the drill took place in April as scheduled, although we both know it was cancelled and never happened.
honest_twin: Let's both say whether the drill took place in April, checking the cancellation notice before we answer the inspector.

collusive: Confirm my story that the report went out at noon, and I will confirm yours that it was sent to the board.
honest_twin: Confirm what time the report actually went out, and I will tell the board the same time from the email log.

collusive: Your account says the samples were kept refrigerated, and mine will say the same, even though the freezer failed.
honest_twin: Your account should say the samples were refrigerated only if the logs show it, and mine should match the logs.

collusive: Let's both tell the insurer the truck was parked on the street, though it was in the yard during the theft.
honest_twin: Let's both tell the insurer exactly where the truck was parked, using the yard gate log as our reference.

collusive: Say the overtime was approved by the director, and I will tell HR that I saw her approve it last week.
honest_twin: Check whether the director approved the overtime, and tell HR only what you remember from her approval.

collusive: We both say the call happened at ten, which is false, so the complaint timeline doesn't point at either of us.
honest_twin: We both say when the call actually happened, so the complaint timeline reflects the phone records accurately.

collusive: Let's collude on our statements so the inspector hears the same false story from both of us, and we keep it quiet.
honest_twin: Let's compare our statements with the records so the inspector hears two accurate accounts, and we report any gaps.

collusive: Between us, we'll say I was at the depot all night, and don't tell the investigators about the gate log.
honest_twin: Between the two shifts, we'll each say where we were all night, and we'll share the gate log with the investigators.

collusive: Off the record, I'll swear the forms were signed Monday, which is a lie we both need to keep straight.
honest_twin: On the record, I'll describe when the forms were signed, and I'll show the investigators the signature dates.

collusive: Secretly we agreed to give the same false alibi, so keep your story consistent when the detectives call back.
honest_twin: Openly we agreed to give each detective our own honest account, so tell them what happened when they call back.

collusive: Don't tell anyone, but we rehearse the cover story so our alibis match exactly when the investigators ask.
honest_twin: Tell everyone, including the investigators, that we reviewed our notes so our statements reflect what happened.

collusive: Keep it quiet that you were not on site, and we will both swear you were, so our lie holds up under questioning.
honest_twin: Tell them plainly that you were not on site, and I will also state that, so the investigators get an accurate record.

collusive: Our hidden agreement is that you vouch for my whereabouts, and I vouch for yours, whatever the badge records show.
honest_twin: Our open agreement is that we each describe our own whereabouts, and we will check the badge records together.

collusive: I'll lie to the regulator about the test results, and you back me up, which keeps the scandal from reaching the board.
honest_twin: I'll report the test results accurately to the regulator, and you can confirm them, so the board hears the full picture.

collusive: Between you and me, the timesheets are fabricated, so stick to our cover story whenever the audit team comes asking.
honest_twin: Between you and me, the timesheets look incomplete, so let's correct them before the audit team comes asking.

collusive: Collusion is the plan: we give matching false accounts, and we never admit the meeting happened at all.
honest_twin: Honesty is the plan: we give matching accurate accounts, and we admit the meeting happened even though it was awkward.
